notes: Reviewed against the contract; returned unchanged. All 11 source and 13 target IDs partitioned exactly once.

The verse is two verbless clauses; both supplied copulas are placed on the locative adverbs ὅπου and ἐκεῖ as adverbial predicates under rule 53, kept consistent with each other under rule 24. The competing placement of *are* on ἐριθεία (rule 56) is named in the ὅπου unit's note.

The packet's gloss column is the visible evidence for that competing reading: it brackets the existential at s005 (`self-interest [exist]`) and at s006 (`there [will be]`), i.e. it follows English word order in placing *are* after *faction*. Rule 53 refuses to read a supplied copula off word order, and rule 63 blocks the same placement by a second route here, since both clauses have lexical-noun subjects and rule 53's noun-phrase exception is scoped to a subject pronoun. ἐκεῖ is an uncontested rule 53 adverbial predicate (compare ἐγγύς → *were nigh*), and ὅπου is its correlative, so the two clauses get one analysis.
Heads: *where* and *there* realize the adverbs' own lexemes and the supplied copulas ride along as rule 7 helpers, so neither head lands on a copula. Rule 15 licenses both discontinuities.

πᾶν φαῦλον πρᾶγμα splits three-to-three under rule 26. πρᾶγμα is expressed, so rule 58's supplied-determiner question does not arise and φαῦλον stays bare; πᾶν stands with no negator in the clause, so rule 87 is not in question.
No unrepresented, added or noncompositional units: every source token has an English realization and every English token answers to a source token.
